subject: Private deployment eligibility + success criteria — post-call recap
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Zhang <ezhang@midstatebank.com>, Tom Peterson <t.peterson@midstatebank.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-28T14:05:00Z
Subject: Private deployment eligibility + success criteria — post-call recap

Elaine / Tom — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and the next-step ask so we can scope an accurate pilot for Midstate Bank.

Key pain points you shared:
- Regulated data residency: PII and transaction logs must remain in Midstate-controlled VPC/region; no egress of raw logs.
- Customer-managed keys (BYOK): KMS integration is mandatory for encryption-at-rest and key rotation policy.
- Air-gap considerations for certain environments: a fully isolated staging environment during validation, with controlled package import processes.
- Network constraints: strict outbound firewall rules, only specific IP ranges allowed, and long procurement lead time for cross-account peering or Direct Connect.
- Auditability: per-request audit logs and retention of model inference metadata for 7+ years for compliance.

Current stack notes (from call):
- Primary infra: on-prem VMware -> core services on K8s (OpenShift in some clusters).
- KMS: in-house HashiCorp Vault with HSM-backed key storage.
- Networking: Palo Alto edge, strict egress, and existing private connectivity to AWS.

Success criteria for a pilot (what you told us):
1) Demonstrate model inference inside your VPC (no routing through public Redwood-hosted endpoints).
2) KMS integration & proof of key control (you can revoke keys and we still maintain auditability).
3) Latency/throughput within agreed SLO (pilot target: 95th percentile end-to-end inference < 250ms for standard prompts).
4) Automated audit logs shipped to your secure SIEM and retention policy validated.
5) Security review pass: SOC2 + network & architecture signoff.

Suggested next steps (what we propose):
- Action 1: We share a concise Mutual Action Plan (attached) with timeline options for an on-prem/VPC pilot. (Owner: me)
- Action 2: You send a sanitized network diagram and the list of allowed outbound IP ranges. This lets us validate NAT/egress requirements and propose connection patterns. (Owner: Midstate)
- Action 3: Vanilla KMS handshake: we’ll provide a short integration spec for HashiCorp Vault/HSMs; your infra team can review. (Owner: Vanessa)
- Action 4: Compliance packet: we’ll attach our SOC2 and SOC2 scoping checklist for enterprise-private deploys.
- Action 5: Follow-up call later this week to align timelines and named resources.

Attachments included: MAP-Midstate-20260528.xlsx (mutual action plan draft), redwood-private-arch-draft.pdf (initial architecture notes).

Open questions from our side that I flagged on the call:
- Can you confirm whether the Vault instance is reachable from a Redwood-hosted service or whether we need a bring-your-binary approach during the air-gap validation?
- Do you have a preferred schedule window for the pilot (e.g., calendar weeks in Q3)?

If agreeable, I’ll send a calendar invite for a 30-minute technical alignment with your infra and security leads. Thanks — looking forward to progressing.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: Private deployment eligibility + success criteria — post-call recap

Thanks Karthik — this is a good summary. A couple clarifications and items from our side: 

Clarifications:
- Vault is HSM-backed and currently only reachable from our internal management network. We do not expose it publicly; any integration will need to be via our cross-account peering or a short-lived connector hosted in our VPC.
- Air-gap: we do not require total physical isolation for the pilot but we do require a sealed validation window where no external artifacts are pulled; packages must be checksum-verified.

Priority asks from Midstate: 
1) KMS integration spec and list of minimal endpoints required so our security team can pre-approve firewall rules.
2) Example network diagram showing how Redwood would deploy a private control plane into our account (we prefer diagrams with minimum set of IAM roles and subnet layout).
3) A concise SPIKE plan for the air-gap validation (what files will be transferred, how signatures are verified).

Timeline: our target is a Q3 pilot kickoff; procurement needs an estimate of effort (FTE days) and a draft quote to start budget approval.

I’m attaching a short PDF that lists our network constraints and current peering notes (midstate-network-constraints.pdf). Tom will be your technical lead for the initial validation.

Tom — can you confirm availability this week for a 30-minute align?

Thanks,
Elaine
Director, Cloud Security | Midstate Bank
ezhang@midstatebank.com | +1 (612) 555-2100

4) Vanessa — please own booking the technical alignment with Tom (Midstate) and our solutions engineering (SE) — recommend 30 minutes this week.

I’ll update the HubSpot deal with the timeline and attach the MAP.

Thanks — targeting to have the MAP + KMS spec ready before the call.
